sectionsUsed: PostgreSQL Downloads: ready-to-use packages or installers for Linux, macOS, Windows, BSD and Solaris, or a source archive; links to the per-system pages used by the 'Now on your own computer' routes
1.1 Installation: PostgreSQL must be installed before use, may already be installed, and can be installed by an unprivileged user
1.1: a pre-packaged installation includes provisions to start the server (install routes)
1.3 Creating a Database: a running PostgreSQL server can manage many databases, typically one per project or user (o1 teaching)
1.3: errors when the server is not running or the role does not exist; PostgreSQL user names are separate from operating system accounts
1.4 Accessing a Database: psql is the interactive terminal program; psql mydb connects; without a name it defaults to the user account name (o2, simulator behavior for bare psql)
1.4: greeting 'psql (18.6)' and 'Type "help" for help.', prompt mydb=> or mydb=# for a superuser; SELECT version(); output format used by the simulator
1.4: internal commands begin with a backslash and are not SQL; \q quits psql (o3)
psql options -d dbname, -h host, -p port (default usually 5432), -U username (simulator options, cheat sheet)
psql: commands are sent at the command-terminating semicolon; an end of line does not terminate a command (continuation prompt, %R in PROMPT2)
Meta-commands \l (list databases), \dt and \d [pattern] (list and describe relations), \q (quit) (o3)
macOS packages: Postgres.app is a native macOS app; open the app and a PostgreSQL server is ready and awaiting connections; close it and the server shuts down (macOS route and its Start recovery)
Windows installers: the interactive installer by EDB includes the PostgreSQL server, pgAdmin and StackBuilder, tested for PostgreSQL 18 (Windows route)
Ubuntu: apt install postgresql installs the distribution's PostgreSQL; postgresql-client-NN holds the client binaries and postgresql-NN the core server (Linux route)

pg_isready checks the connection status of a server: exit 0 accepting connections, 2 no response (server check); printed text 'localhost:5432 - accepting connections' / 'no response' confirmed against a real pg_isready 18.3
18.3: pre-packaged versions include provisions for running the server as a background task (route Expect steps)
18.3.2 Client Connection Problems: 'Connection refused ... Is the server running on that host and accepting TCP/IP connections?' means no server is listening (server-not-running recovery)

Authentication Problems: 'password authentication failed for user', and 'database ... does not exist' (defaults to the user name) (authentication and wrong-database recovery); PostgreSQL 18.3 words a missing user as 'role "..." does not exist', confirmed against a real server
